title: Giving Freely, Not Under Pressure
overview: Paul urges the church in Corinth to finish the gift they promised for poor believers in Jerusalem, and to give it gladly rather than grudgingly.

parts.label: Paul's boast and the advance team (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Paul had told the churches in Macedonia (northern Greece) that the Corinthians in Achaia (southern Greece) had been ready to give since last year, and that news spurred the Macedonians on. Now he sends Titus and two companions ahead, so that if any Macedonians come with him, the gift is already gathered and given freely, not squeezed out at the last minute.

parts.label: Sowing and reaping (vv. 6-7)
parts.note: Paul uses a farming picture: a farmer who plants only a few seeds gets a small harvest. He asks each person to decide for themselves what to give, without pressure, saying God loves a cheerful giver, a line that seems to echo the old Greek translation of Proverbs.

parts.label: God supplies the giver (vv. 8-11)
parts.note: Paul quotes Psalm 112 about a generous person whose goodness lasts, and echoes Isaiah's image of God giving both seed to plant and bread to eat. His point seems to be that God gives people enough to live on and still keep giving, though readers differ on how far this promise reaches beyond simply having enough.

parts.label: Thanks spreading outward (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: The gift meets real needs, and it also leads those who receive it to thank God and pray warmly for the givers. Many scholars think Paul also hoped this gift from non-Jewish churches would show the Jewish believers in Jerusalem that they truly belonged together.

parts.label: A gift beyond words (v. 15)
parts.note: Paul closes by thanking God for a gift too great to describe. Christians have most often read this as Jesus himself, though some think Paul means the generosity God stirred up in these churches.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether the promise that generous sowers will reap generously (vv. 6-11) points to material reward for giving or mainly to having enough, growing in goodness, and being able to keep giving.
think: What makes the difference for you between giving that feels free and giving that feels pressured?
